title: The Nansen Alternative for Funds and Syndicates
content_html:
Why fund managers need a single view of many wallets

You often see your fund’s assets split across many wallets. You may have some on Ethereum, some on MultiversX, and some on other chains. You cannot see the full picture in one place. This makes reporting hard and can hide risk. A clear view helps you make better decisions and keep investors happy.

What Nansen does well

Nansen gives deep on‑chain analytics. It shows which addresses hold large tokens. It tags smart contracts and labels known traders. It lets you follow token flows and spot trends. For a fund that only needs wallet intelligence, Nansen is a strong tool.

Where a broader tool adds value

When you run a crypto fund or a syndicate, you need more than analytics. You need to track many wallets, across many chains, without moving your funds into a custodian. You also need to manage raises, vesting schedules, and on‑chain distributions. You need a place to store investor contacts and run OTC deals.

A platform that lets you track MultiversX and Ethereum wallets in one dashboard while also handling fund administration can fill the gap. It lets you see all assets, no matter which wallet provider you use. It lets you run a raise, set a vesting schedule, and send a distribution, all from the same screen. It keeps your funds in your own wallets, so you stay non‑custodial.

How the all‑in‑one approach works

  • Multi‑chain portfolio: The dashboard shows balances on every EVM chain and on MultiversX. You add wallets from any provider and see them together.
  • Fund raise tools: You create a raise pool, set contribution limits, and collect funds directly in your wallets.
  • Vesting and distribution: You upload a token vesting schedule and let the system release tokens automatically. You can also send on‑chain payouts to investors.
  • Investor CRM: You keep a list of investors, their allocations, and contact info in Groups. This helps you communicate and report.
  • OTC and broker trades: You can record OTC deals and off‑platform broker trades without moving assets into a custodial account.

These pieces work together in a single interface. You do not need to jump between separate apps. You can run a fund, manage a syndicate, and still have the deep wallet insights that Nansen provides.

Why the combination matters for syndicates

Syndicates often pull capital from many investors. They need to see each investor’s share, the total fund exposure, and the performance across chains. They also need to comply with reporting rules. Having a tool that track MultiversX and Ethereum wallets in one dashboard helps them keep everything aligned.

A single view reduces manual spreadsheets. It also lowers the chance of errors when moving tokens between wallets. It lets you focus on sourcing deals instead of juggling data.

Real‑world use case

Imagine a syndicate that invests in DeFi projects on Ethereum and NFT projects on MultiversX. The manager adds multiple Ethereum wallets and several MultiversX wallets to the dashboard. The dashboard shows a substantial net asset value. The manager creates a raise for a new project, sets a multi‑month vesting schedule, and invites investors through Groups. After the raise, the manager runs an OTC trade to acquire a token on MultiversX. All steps are recorded in the same place. The manager can export a report that shows each investor’s share, the vesting timeline, and the current holdings across both chains.

Soft closing

If you need more than on‑chain analytics and want to track MultiversX and Ethereum wallets in one dashboard, you might want to check out cryptool. It lets you keep control of your assets while adding fund administration tools in the same view.
